name: Hakodate
tagline: A harbor city of million-dollar night views and a morning market
intro: Hakodate is a small harbor city at the southern tip of Hokkaido, with the sea on both sides. The night view from Mt. Hakodate, the Western-style churches on the Motomachi hill roads, seafood rice bowls at the Morning Market, the star-shaped fort Goryokaku and Yunokawa Onsen are all within walking distance or a streetcar ride, which makes it a great fit for a first 3-day, 2-night Hokkaido trip or a relaxed trip for couples or a mother and daughter. In winter the highlights are the snowy warehouse district and the monkey hot spring, in spring the cherry blossoms at Goryokaku, and in summer a lakeside stroll at Onuma Park.
season_notes: Spring (late April to early May): the 1,500 cherry trees at Goryokaku peak, with night illuminations. / Summer (June to August): cool weather and squid in season; the harbor festival and fireworks in early August. / Autumn (October to November): fall colors at Onuma Park and Goryokaku. Note that the ropeway closes for its periodic inspection from late October to early November. / Winter (December to February): the snowy warehouse district illuminations and the monkey hot spring. Winds are strong, so dress warmly for the night view observatory.
airport_access/0/note: Runs in time with flight arrivals. Trips that pass through Yunokawa Onsen take about 30 minutes. Check before boarding whether transit IC cards are accepted (contactless payment is announced).
airport_access/1/note: The cheapest way. With lots of luggage, the shuttle bus is easier.
airport_access/2/note: Fare is an estimate. If you are staying at a hot spring hotel, a taxi straight from the airport is the fastest.
getting_around: Two streetcar (shiden) lines connect Yunokawa Onsen, Goryokaku-koen-mae, Hakodate Eki-mae, Jujigai (Motomachi and the Bay Area), and Hakodate Dock-mae and Yachigashira. From the Jujigai stop you can walk around Motomachi, the Bay Area, and the foot of the Mt. Hakodate Ropeway. Onuma Park is about 35 to 40 minutes (¥680) by JR Hakodate Line local train, and you reach the summit of Mt. Hakodate by ropeway or the evening mountain-climbing bus. From Hakodate Station to the Bay Area it is a 15-minute walk, which is often quicker than other options when the weather is good.
transport_pass: Streetcar 1-day pass: ¥800 for adults, ¥400 for children (prices after the December 2025 fare increase; on the smartphone version, show the ticket screen when you get off). Streetcar and Hakodate Bus combined 1-day pass: ¥1,600 for adults. If you ride the streetcar three or more times, the 1-day pass pays off (¥250 to ¥300 per ride).
spots/0/desc: A small airport 9 km east of the city, with domestic and international flights in the same building. Shuttle buses and local buses to Hakodate Station leave right in front of the arrivals floor.
spots/0/access: Shuttle bus to Hakodate Station 20 min, ¥700; Route 96 local bus about 33 min, ¥340
spots/0/tip: Before you depart, you can buy Hasegawa Store yakitori bento (airport branch) and Snaffle's Cheese Omelet at the shop on the 2nd floor. International flights have few check-in counters, so arrive 2 hours before departure.
spots/0/kid_tip: You can watch takeoffs and landings from the observation deck, a nice way to pass waiting time.
spots/1/desc: The terminus of the Hakodate Line and the transit hub where streetcars, buses, and the airport shuttle meet. The Morning Market is right across the station plaza, and the Bay Area is a 15-minute walk away.
spots/1/access: Terminal stop of the airport shuttle bus. 2-minute walk to the Hakodate Eki-mae streetcar stop
spots/1/hours: Matches train times (gates open around 06:00 to around 22:00)
spots/1/tip: The tourist information center inside the station gives out streetcar 1-day passes and maps. Coin lockers are on the 1st floor of the station and on the Morning Market side.
spots/1/kid_tip: The 2nd-floor waiting room has wide windowsides that are comfortable for resting with a stroller.
spots/2/desc: The departure station of the ropeway that climbs to the summit of Mt. Hakodate, on top of the Motomachi hill. A 125-person gondola reaches the summit in about 3 minutes, and the 1st floor has a ticket counter and a souvenir shop.
spots/2/access: 10-minute walk uphill from the Jujigai streetcar stop. About 10 minutes by ropeway shuttle bus from Hakodate Station
spots/2/hours: 10:00–21:00 (Oct 1 to mid-April; last ascent 20:30) / 10:00–22:00 (Apr 20 to Sep 30; last ascent 21:30)
spots/2/closed: Closed for statutory inspection from October 20 to November 8, 2026 (extra mountain-climbing buses run during this period)
spots/2/tip: The most recent information lists the round-trip fare as ¥1,800 for adults and ¥900 for children, but figures differ from site to site, so check the official notice before boarding. The ascent about 40 minutes before sunset is the most crowded, so go up 1 hour before to see both the daytime view and the night view.
spots/2/kid_tip: Strollers can ride the gondola as they are. It is windy at the summit, so bring one extra layer for your child.
spots/3/desc: From the 334 m summit, the lights of the city, pinched narrowly between the seas on both sides, spread out like a fan. Called one of the world's three great night views along with Naples and Hong Kong, it is the heart of a Hakodate trip.
spots/3/access: 3 minutes by ropeway. From late April to early November in the evening, the mountain-climbing bus from Hakodate Eki-mae takes about 30 minutes (about ¥500). In the daytime there are hours when private cars and taxis are restricted.
spots/3/closed: During the ropeway inspection period (October 20 to November 8, 2026) it is reachable by bus only.
spots/3/tip: The best moment is about 30 minutes after sunset, when the sky is deep navy. When it is foggy you cannot see anything, so if the weather is clear on your first day, go up right away instead of putting it off. Window seats at the summit restaurant are by reservation.
spots/3/kid_tip: You can watch from the indoor viewing windows and the rest area on the 1st floor of the observatory, out of the cold.
spots/4/desc: A shopping and dining district that keeps the Meiji-era harbor warehouses as they were, with glassware, music box, and Hokkaido goods shops plus the Hakodate Beer Hall. At night the warehouse walls are lit up, and the canal-side promenade gives the best photos.
spots/4/access: 5-minute walk from the Jujigai streetcar stop. 15-minute walk from Hakodate Station
spots/4/closed: Open year-round (some winter maintenance closure days)
spots/4/tip: In December, the Christmas Fantasy event puts a giant tree in the sea in front of the warehouses. The music box shop and the Snaffle's shop are good places to buy gifts.
spots/4/kid_tip: The wide indoor passages make it a good stroller walk on rainy days. Kids can run around on the lawn plaza in front of the warehouses.
spots/5/desc: Looking down from the top of the hill, the stone-paved road leads straight to Hakodate Harbor and the moored Mashu Maru, making this Hakodate's signature photo spot. Trees and Western-style buildings line both sides, and the snowy winter scene is famous too.
spots/5/access: 3-minute walk from the Suehirocho streetcar stop
spots/5/tip: To avoid backlight in the morning, 2 to 4 p.m. is best, or the evening when the warehouse district lights are on. The slope is steep, so wear low-heeled shoes.
spots/5/kid_tip: Watch out for cars when taking photos on the road at the top of the hill.
spots/6/name: Hakodate Orthodox Church of the Resurrection
spots/6/desc: A Russian Orthodox church with white walls and a green roof, built in 1916; its bell chimes are on Japan's list of 100 Soundscapes. The Catholic Motomachi Church and St. John's Church stand right beside it, so you can see all three churches in one go.
spots/6/access: 10-minute walk from the Jujigai streetcar stop. Right below the Ropeway Sanroku Station
spots/6/hours: To be confirmed (usually 10:00–17:00, until 16:00 on Sat, 13:00–16:00 on Sun)
spots/6/closed: To be confirmed (worship times; partly closed in winter)
spots/6/tip: A donation of around ¥200 is requested for interior viewing. Photography is allowed outside only. The view of the church from Daisanzaka slope is the prettiest.
spots/6/kid_tip: The interior is a place for quiet viewing, so with toddlers it is best to look at the bell tower from outside.
spots/7/name: Former Public Hall of Hakodate Ward
spots/7/desc: A wooden Western-style building built in 1910 with pale yellow and blue exterior walls, designated an Important Cultural Property. The 2nd-floor balcony overlooks the harbor, and inside you can try on rented dresses.
spots/7/access: 7-minute walk from the Suehirocho streetcar stop. Right above Motomachi Park
spots/7/hours: Apr–Oct: Tue–Fri 09:00–18:00, Sat–Mon 09:00–19:00 / Nov–Mar: 09:00–17:00 (last entry 30 minutes before closing)
spots/7/closed: December 31 to January 3 (some in-house maintenance days)
spots/7/tip: The combined ticket with the Former British Consulate, the Northern Peoples Museum and others (2 sites ¥500, 3 sites ¥720) is a good deal. The dress experience is paid in 20-minute units.
spots/7/kid_tip: The dress experience has kids' sizes too, so it is a nice activity with a daughter.
spots/8/desc: A consulate building built in 1913, now used as a port-opening memorial museum, with a tearoom and rose garden where you can enjoy afternoon tea. There is also a shop selling British goods.
spots/8/access: 5-minute walk from the Suehirocho streetcar stop
spots/8/tip: Roses peak from mid-June to early July. The tearoom can be used without an admission fee, and the scone set is popular.
spots/8/kid_tip: The garden is flat, so it is easy for kids to walk.
spots/9/desc: A terraced park below the Former Public Hall with a viewpoint that takes in the harbor and the Bay Area at a glance. Cherry blossoms are pretty in spring and ginkgo leaves in autumn, and there is a tourist information center inside the park.
spots/9/access: 5-minute walk up the Motoizaka slope from the Suehirocho streetcar stop
spots/9/tip: If you make this the starting point for your Motomachi hill walk, the route goes downhill, which is easier.
spots/9/kid_tip: There are benches and restrooms, so it is a good place to rest.
spots/10/desc: A small museum collecting clothing and daily tools of the Ainu and other northern minority peoples, housed in a former Bank of Japan branch building. A good stop between the Bay Area and Motomachi on a rainy day.
spots/10/access: 1-minute walk from the Suehirocho streetcar stop
spots/10/tip: Cheaper if bundled in the combined ticket with the Former Public Hall. Postcards with Ainu embroidery patterns make good souvenirs.
spots/10/kid_tip: There are few hands-on corners, so it suits upper elementary school kids and older rather than toddlers.
spots/11/desc: A market of about 250 stalls right next to Hakodate Station, famous for Donburi Yokocho, lined with seafood rice bowl restaurants, and for its squid-fishing tanks. You can buy melon, crab, and sea urchin and eat them on the spot or ship them home.
spots/11/access: 2-minute walk from the west exit of JR Hakodate Station
spots/11/hours: Roughly 05:00–14:00 (from 06:00 in Jan–Apr; varies by stall)
spots/11/tip: The busiest time is 7 to 9 a.m., and after 10 more shops close. Squid fishing costs around ¥1,500 to ¥2,000 per squid (market price), and it is served right away as sashimi.
spots/11/kid_tip: The squid-fishing experience is the kids' favorite. The aisles are narrow, so bring a baby carrier rather than a stroller.
spots/12/desc: A 5-minute walk from Hakodate Station, an alley of 26 small food stalls where you can go from stall to stall tasting a plate or two of Genghis Khan (grilled lamb), squid sashimi, shio ramen, and skewers. The lights come on around 6 p.m., and the atmosphere picks up.
spots/12/access: 5-minute walk from JR Hakodate Station. 2-minute walk from the Matsukazecho streetcar stop
spots/12/hours: 11:00–01:00 (most open around 17:00 to 18:00; varies by stall)
spots/12/tip: With 6 to 10 seats per stall, groups of 2 to 3 are best. Bring cash. A bowl of shio ramen at Ryuho is the classic finish.
spots/12/kid_tip: Some stalls have cigarette smoke, so with kids stick to ramen shops early in the evening (before 6 p.m.).
spots/13/desc: From the observation deck of the 107 m tower you can see the whole star-shaped fortress Goryokaku, Mt. Hakodate, and the Tsugaru Strait in 360 degrees. The 1st floor has a Hakodate souvenir shop and a cafe.
spots/13/access: 10-minute walk from the Goryokaku-koen-mae streetcar stop
spots/13/hours: 09:00–18:00 (observation tickets sold until 17:50; extended during Golden Week and cherry blossom season)
spots/13/tip: During cherry blossom season (late April to early May) and the winter fortress illumination (evenings from December to February), opening hours are extended. For the glass-floor spot on the deck, go right after opening when the line is short.
spots/13/kid_tip: Elementary school students ¥600, preschoolers free. The model exhibits on the deck explain the fort's history in an easy way.
spots/14/desc: A Western-style star-shaped fortress site built in the late Edo period, with 1,500 cherry trees planted along the moat, making it Hokkaido's top cherry blossom spot. Inside the fort is the restored Hakodate Bugyosho, and you can ride a boat on the moat.
spots/14/access: 10-minute walk from the Goryokaku-koen-mae streetcar stop. Right next to Goryokaku Tower
spots/14/tip: The walking path around the moat is about 1.8 km, 30 minutes. The night illumination in cherry blossom season runs from around 19:00 to 21:00.
spots/14/kid_tip: From spring to autumn there are moat boats (paid) and a wide lawn, so kids can run around.
spots/15/desc: A government office of the Edo shogunate, restored in 2010 with traditional methods in the center of Goryokaku, where you can walk through the tatami rooms and wooden corridors as they were. Videos explain the Battle of Hakodate and how the fort was built.
spots/15/access: Inside Goryokaku Park, 10-minute walk from the tower
spots/15/hours: Apr–Oct 09:00–18:00, Nov–Mar 09:00–17:00 (last admission 15 minutes before closing)
spots/15/tip: You take your shoes off to go in, so bring socks. Visiting right after the tower viewing makes a tidy route.
spots/15/kid_tip: Free for preschoolers. The wooden floors are slippery, so remind kids not to run.
spots/16/name: Yunokawa Onsen Foot Bath Yumeguri Butai
spots/16/desc: A free foot bath right in front of the Yunokawa Onsen streetcar stop, the starting point for a stroll through the 350-year-old Yunokawa hot spring district. Hot spring hotels line the seaside, and since it is 10 minutes from the airport, it is a popular choice for the last night.
spots/16/access: Right in front of the Yunokawa Onsen streetcar stop. About 30 minutes by streetcar from Hakodate Station
spots/16/tip: Bring a small towel. Most hotels in the hot spring district accept day-use bathing (around ¥1,000 to ¥1,500), so you can stop by without staying overnight.
spots/16/kid_tip: The water is on the hot side, so kids should dip their feet only briefly. There is a convenience store right next door.
spots/17/desc: The shrine at the origin of Yunokawa Onsen, with rabbit statues from the legend of discovering the hot spring placed all around the grounds. The rabbit-shaped charms and omikuji fortunes are cute and popular with women travelers.
spots/17/access: 3-minute walk from the Yunokawa streetcar stop (terminus)
spots/17/tip: The rabbit omikuji comes with the paper placed inside a rabbit doll, so it is nice to take home as a souvenir.
spots/17/kid_tip: The grounds are flat and small, so it is easy to go around with a stroller.
spots/18/name: Hakodate City Tropical Botanical Garden (Monkey Hot Spring)
spots/18/desc: A greenhouse botanical garden on the Yunokawa Onsen seaside, famous in winter (December to early May) for more than 70 Japanese macaques soaking in the hot spring bath. In summer, a water play area and rides open.
spots/18/access: 15-minute walk from the Yunokawa Onsen streetcar stop. 5 minutes by taxi from the airport
spots/18/tip: Admission is cash only. The monkey bathing period and times change every year, so check the official notice. You can feed the monkeys (paid).
spots/18/kid_tip: Elementary and middle school students ¥100, preschoolers free. For summer water play, bring a change of clothes and a towel.
spots/19/desc: Japan's first women's monastery, founded in 1898, with a red brick chapel and garden paths open to the public. The madeleines and butter candy made by the nuns are famous as souvenirs.
spots/19/access: About 15 minutes by bus or 10 minutes by taxi from Yunokawa Onsen. 7 minutes by taxi from the airport
spots/19/hours: To be confirmed (usually 08:10–17:00, winter 08:30–16:30; building interior closed to the public)
spots/19/closed: To be confirmed (shop closed December 30 to January 2)
spots/19/tip: It is close to the airport, so it is nice to visit on the morning of departure. The madeleines at the shop sometimes sell out in the afternoon.
spots/19/kid_tip: The garden stairs are long, so a baby carrier is better than a stroller. It is a place for quiet walking.
spots/20/desc: A scenic spot on a cliff at the southern tip of Mt. Hakodate, with views of the Tsugaru Strait and the Shimokita Peninsula. On the way is the family grave of the poet Ishikawa Takuboku, and in summer rugosa roses bloom.
spots/20/access: 15-minute uphill walk from the Yachigashira streetcar stop (terminus). A taxi is easier.
spots/20/closed: Road closed from November to late March (snow and strong winds)
spots/20/tip: The wind is very strong, so watch your hat and skirt. Pair it with Yachigashira Onsen for a half-day course.
spots/20/kid_tip: There is a railing at the cliff edge, but hold your child's hand firmly.
spots/21/desc: A sightseeing boat that leaves from the pier in front of the Kanemori Warehouses and circles the harbor for 30 minutes. From the sea side you can get a photo that takes in the warehouse district and Mt. Hakodate together.
spots/21/access: At the pier right in front of the Kanemori Warehouses
spots/21/hours: To be confirmed (operates late April to October; several 30-minute daytime cruises and a 60-minute evening night cruise)
spots/21/tip: The sunset night cruise is an alternative for days when you cannot go to the night view observatory. Buy tickets at the pier on the day.
spots/21/kid_tip: There are indoor seats, so it is fine even when the wind blows.
spots/22/desc: One of Japan's oldest parks, opened in 1879, with a small amusement park, Kodomo no Kuni, where Japan's oldest Ferris wheel turns, and a mini zoo. During the spring cherry blossom festival, stalls line the paths.
spots/22/access: 3-minute walk from the Aoyagicho streetcar stop
spots/22/hours: Park anytime / Amusement park to be confirmed (daytime from late March to late November, closed in winter)
spots/22/closed: Amusement park closed in winter and in bad weather
spots/22/tip: Rides use a coupon-ticket system at around ¥300 per ride. It is in the same direction as Cape Tachimachi, so the two pair well.
spots/22/kid_tip: It is mostly small rides that toddlers can ride, so preschoolers like it best. The zoo is free.
spots/23/desc: A small station on the Hakodate Line; get off and you are right at the entrance to the Lake Onuma walking path. In front of the station are a tourist information center, a bike rental shop, and the famous Onuma dango shop.
spots/23/access: From Hakodate Station by local train about 35 to 40 minutes, ¥680 (limited express about 30 minutes, limited express ticket extra)
spots/23/tip: Local trains run once every 1 to 2 hours, so take a photo of the return timetable first.
spots/23/kid_tip: You can rent bicycles in front of the station (including ones with child seats).
spots/24/desc: A lake park with 126 large and small islands floating against the backdrop of Mt. Komagatake. Popular activities include 15 to 50 minute walking courses over the bridges linking the islands, sightseeing boats, and the 14 km bike ride around the lake. Autumn leaves and the frozen lake in winter are beautiful.
spots/24/hours: Anytime (boats run regularly May–Oct, irregularly in April, November, and December)
spots/24/tip: The 30-minute island-circuit boat is listed at ¥1,460 for adults and ¥730 for children, but that information is more than 2 years old, so please confirm. The Onuma dango (soy sauce and sweet red bean) from Numanoya in front of the station must be eaten the same day.
spots/24/kid_tip: The island paths are flat, so strollers are fine. Rent a boat or bikes to make a full half-day.
restaurants/0/signature: Original Hakodate Tomoe-don (sea urchin, salmon roe, and scallop trio) ¥3,278
restaurants/0/desc: The original seafood rice bowl restaurant at the Morning Market, founded in 1956, best known for the Tomoe-don where you choose three toppings. It also serves charcoal-grilled fish set meals, so family members who cannot eat raw fish can come along.
restaurants/0/tips/0: No reservations; arriving before 8 a.m. means a shorter wait
restaurants/0/tips/1: Mini-size bowls are available, good for sharing between two
restaurants/0/tips/2: Also has branches at New Chitose Airport and the Bay Area
restaurants/1/cuisine: Seafood rice bowls and set meals
restaurants/1/signature: Live squid sashimi and seafood rice bowl
restaurants/1/desc: A rare place in the Morning Market that stays open until late in the evening, so you can enjoy market seafood even if your flight arrives late. The menu is broad, with squid sashimi, crab miso soup, and grilled set meals.
restaurants/1/tips/0: The place for a Morning Market meal in the evening
restaurants/1/tips/1: Live squid can sell out depending on the market price and supply
restaurants/2/signature: Additive-free fresh sea urchin rice bowl
restaurants/2/desc: A specialty shop run directly by a sea urchin processing company, serving fresh sea urchin without alum as rice bowls, sushi, and grilled dishes. Prices are high, but there is none of the bitterness typical of sea urchin, so even first-timers like it.
restaurants/2/closed: Tuesdays (from January 2026), year-end and New Year holidays
restaurants/2/tips/0: Prices change with the sea urchin market
restaurants/2/tips/2: Last orders for fried and grilled dishes are 15 minutes earlier
restaurants/3/name: Lucky Pierrot Bay Area Main Store
restaurants/3/desc: The first store of a hamburger chain found only in Hakodate, nationally famous for the Chinese Chicken Burger with sweet soy-glazed fried chicken. It also has curry, omurice, and soft serve, so it is easy to go with kids.
restaurants/3/tips/0: Lines at lunch and dinner peaks; you are seated after ordering
restaurants/3/tips/1: One menu item per person is the rule
restaurants/3/tips/2: Each branch has a different interior theme, which is fun to see
restaurants/4/signature: Hakodate local beer set with sausages and squid dishes
restaurants/4/desc: A spacious beer hall inside the Kanemori Warehouses serving four local beers along with seafood, Genghis Khan, and sausages. There are plenty of seats, so it is easy with kids, and at night the mood is lovely with the warehouse lights.
restaurants/4/tips/1: Non-alcoholic drinks and a kids' menu available
restaurants/5/signature: Yakitori bento (pork skewer lunch box), small, around ¥600
restaurants/5/desc: The home convenience store of the Hakodate-style yakitori bento, where skewers are grilled to order and set on top of rice. They are pork skewers, not chicken, and you can choose sauce, salt, or seasoned flavor.
restaurants/5/tips/0: Grilling takes around 10 minutes, so order ahead
restaurants/5/tips/1: Good as a late-night snack at your hotel after the night view
restaurants/5/tips/2: Price is an estimate; check at the store
restaurants/6/desc: The directly run store of Hakodate's signature sweet, the Cheese Omelet, where you can buy gift boxes or single pieces. It is inside the warehouses, so it is easy to drop in while shopping.
restaurants/6/closed: Open year-round (follows the Kanemori Yobutsukan closing days)
restaurants/6/tips/0: Keeps about 10 days refrigerated; buy it the day before you fly home
restaurants/6/tips/1: Also has shops at Hakodate Airport and the station
restaurants/7/signature: Mer Cheese (mini cheesecake) and soft serve
restaurants/7/desc: A pastry shop famous for Mer Cheese mini cheesecakes, one of Hakodate's two big names alongside Snaffle's, with cafe seating where you can also eat fresh cakes. Seasonal flavors such as pumpkin and chocolate are fun.
restaurants/7/tips/0: Mer Cheese can be packed frozen, handy for gifts to take home
restaurants/7/tips/1: The main store is in Toyokawacho, and there is a shop at the airport too
restaurants/8/signature: 30-minute shelf-life chewy crepe (strawberry and fresh cream)
restaurants/8/desc: A small chocolate shop with lines from across the country for its chewy crepes, baked to order and best eaten within 30 minutes. The Chocolat Voyage (fresh chocolate) is also popular as a gift.
restaurants/8/closed: Mondays and Tuesdays (next day if a holiday)
restaurants/8/tips/0: Shorter waits right after opening or after 3 p.m.
restaurants/8/tips/1: Eat the crepe right in front of the shop
restaurants/8/tips/2: Check the official calendar for closing days
restaurants/9/signature: Meiji-era revival curry and beef stew
restaurants/9/desc: Hokkaido's oldest Western-style restaurant, founded in 1879, serving British-style curry and course meals in the retro main building hall. The 1st floor of the shop sells retort curry as gifts.
restaurants/9/closed: Tuesdays (open daily in summer, closed January 1 to 2)
restaurants/9/tips/0: The lunch curry set is good value
restaurants/9/tips/2: Closing days change by season, so confirm by phone
restaurants/10/desc: The main store of the Hakodate sausage brand started by a German craftsman in the 1920s, with freshly made hot dogs on the 1st floor and a history exhibit on the 2nd. A good snack during a hill-road walk.
restaurants/10/tips/0: Check whether vacuum-packed sausages are allowed in the cabin
restaurants/11/desc: A tea room in an old private house built in 1921, where you sip zenzai and green tea in a tatami room overlooking the garden. It is right next to the Motomachi church district, a good place to rest during a walk.
restaurants/11/tips/1: Winter oshiruko (sweet red bean soup) is popular
restaurants/12/desc: An antique cafe converted from a Taisho-era pawnshop storehouse, with stone walls and old furniture full of atmosphere. The anmitsu, cakes, and coffee are all excellent, and it ranks as the number one cafe in Hakodate among women travelers.
restaurants/12/tips/0: 1-minute walk from the Horaicho streetcar stop
restaurants/12/tips/1: Browsing the 1st-floor antique shop is fun too
restaurants/13/signature: Black wagyu sukiyaki course and croquettes from the 1st-floor butcher
restaurants/13/desc: A sukiyaki specialty restaurant founded in 1901, where staff cook authentic sukiyaki for you in a tatami room on the 2nd floor. The handmade croquettes from the butcher on the 1st floor are a snack people line up for.
restaurants/13/closed: To be confirmed (information suggests closed on Wednesdays)
restaurants/13/tips/0: Reservations are a must for dinner
restaurants/13/tips/1: To buy only the croquettes, go to the 1st-floor butcher in the daytime
restaurants/14/desc: A leading Hakodate shio ramen shop with a history going back to the 1930s, right next to Goryokaku Tower. The kelp-based broth is clear and clean, so it is easy for both kids and adults.
restaurants/14/closed: Fourth Wednesday (next weekday if a holiday)
restaurants/14/tips/0: Lines are long from 12 to 1 p.m., so right after the 11 a.m. opening is recommended
restaurants/14/tips/1: Also has branches at Hakodate Station and New Chitose Airport
restaurants/15/signature: Marusei Butter Sand and pizza and cake at the 2nd-floor cafe
restaurants/15/desc: Hakodate base of the Hokkaido confectionery brand Rokkatei, where you enjoy cake and coffee at the 2nd-floor cafe windows overlooking the Goryokaku moat and cherry trees. You can also pick up gift sweets in one stop.
restaurants/15/tips/0: The cafe has long waits in cherry blossom season
restaurants/15/tips/1: Butter Sand keeps at room temperature, so it is easy as a gift
restaurants/16/name: Conveyor Belt Sushi Kantaro Ugaura Main Store
restaurants/16/signature: Hakodate squid, scallop, and salmon roe sushi
restaurants/16/desc: The main store of what is regarded as the originator of Hakodate conveyor belt sushi, with seaside window seats overlooking the Tsugaru Strait. At ¥200 to ¥500 a plate, a family can taste local fish without worrying about cost.

bplan/5/desc: When the kids get bored: small rides and a free zoo (closed in winter)

bplan/6/desc: With a rental car, drive the road around the lake, then on to Yamakawa Farm soft serve
bplan/7/title: Alternatives for Uni Murakami's Closing Day (Kikuyo Shokudo, Yamasan)
bplan/7/desc: When it is closed on Tuesday, substitute a sea urchin or seafood rice bowl at Kikuyo Shokudo or Yamasan Michishita Shokudo in the Morning Market
nearby_alternatives/0/reason: There are far more direct flights, and the choices for a city trip are wider, from the Otaru Canal to Susukino dining
nearby_alternatives/1/reason: One hour from Hakodate by Shinkansen, a quiet destination centered on the Nebuta Festival and Hirosaki cherry blossoms
nearby_alternatives/2/reason: Choose this one if your goals are the Biei and Furano flower fields, Asahiyama Zoo, nature, and driving
checks/0: The Mt. Hakodate Ropeway is closed for statutory inspection from October 20 to November 8, 2026. During this period, use the mountain-climbing bus from Hakodate Eki-mae
checks/1: The night view depends a lot on the weather. If it is clear on your first day, go up that very day, and if it is cloudy, put it off to the next day
checks/2: The Morning Market ends in the morning. If you go late, many shops are closed, so plan it as breakfast
checks/3: Streetcar fares went up in December 2025 (1-day pass ¥800). If you ride three or more times, buy the 1-day pass
checks/4: Many food stalls, markets, and old restaurants accept cash only. Bring ¥20,000 to ¥30,000 in cash per person
checks/5: The sea wind is strong. Bring a windbreaker even in spring and autumn, and in winter non-slip shoes and gloves
checks/6: Set the dinner time at the Yunokawa hot spring hotel when you check in. If your flight is delayed, contact the hotel
checks/7: Local trains to Onuma Park run once every 1 to 2 hours. Check the return train time first
checks/8: Reserve popular restaurants (Uni Murakami, Asari, Goto-ken dinner), and check closing days in the official notice before you visit
checks/9: Direct flights to Hakodate are few depending on season and day of week, so settle your flight schedule first (to be confirmed)
highlights/0: 20 minutes from the airport to the station
highlights/1: One of the world's three great night views
